title: OAuth Readiness Guide — Content Schema
description: PM-authored content contract for a provider OAuth integration guide. This describes WHAT a guide must contain to let a developer decide-and-ship fast, organized around the developer's journey: Decide → Prepare → Build → Verify → Ship. It is the product spec for the guide payload; server plumbing fields (id, slug, timestamps, status, finding back-references) are intentionally omitted — see guide.content.README below. Every factual field follows the honesty contract: a value is present ONLY when backed by retrieved evidence; otherwise it is null/empty and surfaced as an open question. Never fabricate.

provider.description: WHO this guide is about. First thing a developer confirms they're on the right page.

url.description: Provider's own homepage/docs root. http(s) only. Null-equivalent: a search URL when the real one wasn't established — the UI must label that honestly.

summary.description: One-paragraph 'what is this and what can I build with it' — scannable in 5 seconds.

logoUrl.description: Optional brand logo for the card/header. Recognition speeds scanning in the library. Null when not found.

decision.description: DECIDE. The single most important block: which path should I take, and is it worth starting now? A developer should be able to make a go/no-go call from this alone.

recommendedPath.description: managed-auth = use Composio's managed connection (least work); custom-oauth = register your own provider OAuth app; other = a justified non-OAuth route (explain in rationale).

rationale.description: WHY this path, in plain language. Must reference what was actually observed, not generic advice.

alternativePaths.description: Optional. Other viable routes with a one-line trade-off each, so the developer sees the decision space, not just the verdict.

tradeoff.description: e.g. 'More control, but you own token refresh and app review.'

effort.description: DECIDE (cost). Keep hands-on work separate from waiting-on-others — a developer plans very differently for '2 hours of coding' vs '3 days waiting for app review'.

externalWaiting.description: Calendar time blocked on the provider (review, verification, approval).

prerequisites.description: PREPARE. What must already be true before step 1 — accounts, plans, entitlements. Prevents the developer starting and hitting a wall three steps in.

implementation.description: BUILD (reference). The copy-pasteable core: the concrete OAuth facts a developer wires into code. This is the single highest-value block for speed — endpoints, scopes, PKCE, token lifetime, limits. Honesty contract is strict here: a URL appears ONLY if quoted in authoritative evidence; otherwise null, never a pattern-guess.

refreshUrl.description: Token refresh endpoint (often same as tokenUrl).

scopes.description: OAuth scopes relevant to the stated use case. Empty is valid and meaningful (provider may not use scopes) — say so in an open question.

required.description: Required for the stated use case.

redirectUriRule.description: FORMAT/constraints of the redirect URI (e.g. 'https only except http://localhost; must exactly match a registered value') — never a fabricated literal.

limit.description: Kept as a string — providers phrase limits many ways; never coerce into a fabricated number.

scope.description: What it applies to, e.g. 'order placement'.

testMode.description: Sandbox / dev-workspace availability for testing without going to production.

setupSteps.description: BUILD (do). The ordered, actionable spine of the guide, grouped by phase. This is the centerpiece a developer executes top-to-bottom. Each step is self-contained: what to do, what should happen, how to confirm, and what to do if it breaks.

phase.description: Drives the journey grouping. Ordered as listed.

instructions.description: Concrete: where to go, what to click/enter.

rationale.description: Why this step matters (optional, builds trust/understanding).

appliesWhen.description: Condition under which this conditional step applies, e.g. 'only for multi-tenant apps'.

fields.description: Configuration values this step asks the developer to supply/collect. The product's anti-footgun layer: it labels WHERE each value comes from and never asks for or stores secrets.

expectedOutcome.description: What success looks like after this step.

verification.description: How to confirm it actually worked.

recovery.description: What to do if it fails (the step the developer actually needs at 2am).

executionMode.description: Who/what performs this — sets expectation for the agent-vs-human split.

agentVsHuman.description: BUILD (division of labor). This product is for connecting providers to AI AGENTS, so a developer specifically wants to know: what can my agent do unattended vs what needs a human once. Omit entirely rather than guess.

approvalRequirements.description: SHIP. Provider review / verification / distribution gates that stand between 'works in testing' and 'works for real users'. Surfaced separately because they carry calendar time, not code time.

knownBlockers.description: SHIP (risk). Things that will stop or slow a developer — hard dependencies, gotchas, rate-limit cliffs. Shown prominently; the single worst one is promoted into the decision area.

severity.description: PM addition: lets the UI rank and color blockers instead of treating all equally.

nextAction.description: START HERE. The one clearest first move, so a developer who's convinced can act immediately without re-reading the whole guide.

openQuestions.description: TRUST. What the research could NOT establish, stated as questions with how to resolve them. Preserving uncertainty honestly is a product differentiator — a guide that admits gaps beats one that bluffs.

howToResolve.description: Concrete next step to close the gap (e.g. 'check the Composio toolkit catalog').

sources.description: TRUST. Every source consulted, tiered by authority so a developer can weigh claims. The thing that makes this an 'evidence-backed' guide rather than an LLM opinion.

confidence.description: TRUST (at-a-glance). A single honest signal of how grounded this guide is, so the reader calibrates before trusting it.

level.description: high = key facts on authoritative sources; low = mostly third-party/community or many open questions.

basis.description: One line explaining the level, e.g. 'Endpoints confirmed on provider docs; token lifetime unestablished.'

estimate.description: An honest time/quantity estimate. kind states how we know; value/unit are null when genuinely unknown (and must be rendered as 'Unknown', not zero).

description.description: What the provider expects for this field.

provenance.description: Where the value comes from. developer-input = you choose it; environment-derived = from your own app (e.g. redirect URI); provider-issued = the provider gives it to you (e.g. client id). The product NEVER stores provider-issued secrets.

suggestedValue.description: A copyable literal ONLY when quoted in authoritative evidence; null otherwise. Never a secret.

validation.description: How to validate the entered value.

sourceType.description: Authority tier. official-docs / developer-portal are credited ONLY when on the provider's own domain. This tiering is what lets the reader trust (or discount) each claim.

evidenceList.description: Inline citations for a claim: the sources that back it. Empty means the claim is asserted without a cited source — the UI should treat that as weaker.
